empty!(a) removes every element of a valid vector, which stays valid.

pushfirst!(a, item) inserts convert(eltype(a), item) before every old element, which keep their order, in a valid vector, and a failing conversion propagates with a untouched; the memory length plus three must be an Int.

The dequeue contract of array.jl's "Dequeue functionality" (push!, pop!, pushfirst!, popfirst!; docstrings at array.jl:1325-1350, 1654-1694, 1753-1771, 1799-1830) for an item of any type: the `Vector{T}` methods `push!(a, item)` and `pushfirst!(a, item)` (array.jl:1353, 1772) store `item` itself when it is already a `T` and otherwise `convert(T, item)` (user-extensible, a parameter with no law; "convert first so we don't grow the array if the assignment won't work"). When that conversion throws, both `push!` and `pushfirst!` raise its error with the store unchanged. Otherwise `push!(a, item)` followed by `pop!(a)` returns the stored value and leaves `a` with its old contents, and `pushfirst!(a, item)` followed by `popfirst!(a)` does the same at the front, in a valid vector. The precondition is that the memory can grow by one slot at either end.

`copyto!(dest, doffs, src, soffs, n)` (array.jl:288-296 through `_copyto_impl!`; docstring at array.jl:282-287: "Copy `n` elements from collection `src` starting at the linear index `soffs`, to array `dest` starting at the index `doffs`. Otherwise `dest` is returned and its memory holds the copied old source window in place of its own, every other heap object unchanged.

`copyto!(dest, src)` for the seven Array/Memory pairs (array.jl:325-332, through `_copyto2arg!`, array.jl:323: `copyto!(dest, firstindex(dest), src, firstindex(src), length(src))`) for operands of every shape, possibly sharing memory (`copyto!` docstring in abstractarray.jl: "Copy all elements from collection `src` to array `dest`, whose length must be greater than or equal to the length `n` of `src`. A value already of type `T` is stored, otherwise `convert(T, x)` (user-extensible, a parameter with no law) decides: its error propagates with the array unchanged; otherwise every element of `A` becomes the value and `A` is returned (the heap: every slot of its memory, every other heap object unchanged).

copy(::Array) propagates allocation failures with their resulting state. After successful allocation it preserves type, rank, dimensions, payload bytes and union selector bytes, including null reference representations, in a fresh Array header and fresh nonempty memory, while retaining every old live byte. Empty memories may share the runtime singleton. Sizes accepted by unsafe_wrap but rejected by the ordinary allocator retain ArgumentError.

The `similar` methods for `Array` (array.jl:414-421, `similar` docstring in abstractarray.jl: "Create an uninitialized mutable array with the given element type and size, based upon the given source array.") on the shared heap, with `Vector{T}(undef, n)`, `Matrix{T}(undef, n, m)` and `Array{T,N}(undef, dims)` the Core allocators of the store (`heapVectorAllocate`, `heapAllocateIntDims`): each returns a fresh array of the requested element type (the source's element type when none is given) and the requested dimensions (`size(a, 1)`, `size(a, 2)` by default), with only unassigned slots, appended to the heap so that no existing array changes; a negative dimension raises `ArgumentError`.

`n == 0` returns the destination without converting offsets. For any nonzero count, a failed Int conversion of either offset or the count throws an error; otherwise, positive in-bounds windows copy the old source slots, including overlap, while preserving every other heap object. Array lengths are Int-representable.

`vect()` (array.jl:158, the empty literal `[]`; `vect(X...)` docstring at array.jl:168-181: "Create a `Vector` ... containing the argument list") and `getindex(::Type{Any})` (array.jl:471, `Any[]`; docstring at array.jl:424-444: "Construct a 1-d array of the specified type"), each `Vector{Any}()`, through the store's `Array` allocation: every call returns a new valid empty vector whose memory no existing array shares, and every existing array keeps its header and contents.
Homogeneous vector literals contain exactly their arguments in order, including empty inputs.
Typed literals preserve the allocated element type and contain each converted value in order; the first failed conversion propagates, for homogeneous and mixed arguments.
Mixed vector literals have the promoted element type and the arguments converted to that type in order; conversion errors propagate.

Checked linear stores round-trip through reads, preserve other slots and shape, reject exactly out-of-range positions, propagate conversion failures without mutation, and unsetting clears only the selected boxed or pointer-containing inline slot while preserving union and pointer-free raw storage.

`isassigned(a::Array, i::Int...)` (array.jl:231; `isassigned` docstring in abstractarray.jl: "Return `true` if the value at the given index exists in an array, and `false` if it is out of bounds or has an undefined reference") on a heap array, with `checkbounds(Bool, a, i...)` and `_sub2ind(size(a), i...)` of abstractarray.jl: one index per dimension gives `true` exactly when it is in bounds and the slot at its column-major position is assigned; a single linear index gives `true` exactly when it lies in `1:length(a)` and that slot is assigned; no index gives `true` exactly when every dimension is one and the only slot is assigned.

`unsetindex!(A::Array, i::Integer)` (array.jl:208, through `to_index(i)`: indices.jl's `convert(Int, i)`, `ArgumentError` for a `Bool`; and `unsetindex!(A::Array, i::Int)` at array.jl:210) on a vector of the store, for an index of every `Integer` type: a `Bool` raises `ArgumentError`, an index with no equal `Int` `InexactError`, and an index outside `1:length(A)` `BoundsError`, each with the store unchanged; otherwise the selected raw slot of `A` is cleared for boxed or pointer-containing inline storage and preserved for union or pointer-free storage, `A` is returned, and no array header changes.

Inline element strides equal their runtime sizes, boxed arrays use pointer strides, sizeof counts element bytes, pointer strides respect alignment, and bottom-type queries return zero or MethodError for extra arguments.

Given the native stride returned by aligned_sizeof(T), BitInteger and Bool byte counts use installed wrapping multiplication with that stride. For an unmodelled Integer, multiplication may throw or return a native BitInteger or opaque Integer. An error outcome throws; native results use Csize_t conversion, opaque results use the type's conversion, and successful valid windows copy the converted byte count with other bytes unchanged.
DimensionMismatch() has an empty message; empty vcat and hcat allocate a zero-length Vector{Any} with no readable index.

A[r] for an Int range reads A[i] for i in r in order; the first index outside 1:length(A) raises BoundsError and the first unassigned slot UndefRefError before anything is built; otherwise the comprehension builder receives exactly the values A[i] in order.

A[I] = X raises DimensionMismatch unless length(X) == length(I), then BoundsError for an index outside 1:length(A), with nothing changed; otherwise each X[k], converted, is stored at A[I[k]] in order (a repeated index keeps its last value) and every other slot and memory is unchanged; an unassigned X[k] or failing conversion raises after X[1:k-1] are stored.

insert!(a, i, item) for an index of any BitInteger type converts item first (errors propagate with a untouched), raises InexactError when i is not an Int value and BoundsError outside 1:length(a)+1 with a untouched, and otherwise puts the converted item at index i with the old elements before and after it in order.
push!(a::Vector{Any}, x...) appends the values after every old element and pushfirst!(a::Vector{Any}, x...) inserts them before, in argument order, in a valid vector.
append!(a, items) for a Vector items makes a its old elements followed by the elements items had before the call (unassigned slots included), items == a doubling a, in a valid vector.
prepend!(a, items) for a Vector items makes a the elements items had before the call followed by its old elements (unassigned slots included), items == a doubling a, in a valid vector.

sizehint!(a, sz; first, shrink) for sz of any BitInteger type raises InexactError when sz is not an Int value, and otherwise returns a with exactly the same elements in a valid vector, whether it shrinks, grows at the front or end, or leaves the memory, with no other header changed.

For representation-valid storage (pointer-free slots are assigned) and strictly increasing Int indices inside 1:length(a), deleteat!(a, inds) keeps exactly the other slots in order (unassigned included) and splice!(a, inds) also returns a fresh vector of the removed slots in order; a first index outside 1:length(a) or a later one above length(a) raises BoundsError and a later index not above its predecessor raises ArgumentError.

splice!(a, i, ins) for an Int index raises BoundsError outside 1:length(a) and UndefRefError for an unassigned a[i], with nothing changed; otherwise with all replacements converting it returns a[i] and leaves a[1:i-1], the converted replacements, then a[i+1:end]; a failing conversion raises its error.

splice!(a, lo:hi, ins) for an Int range raises BoundsError for a nonempty range outside 1:length(a) (nothing changed) and for an insertion point n:n-1 outside 1:length(a)+1 with replacements; otherwise with all replacements converting it returns a fresh vector of a[lo:hi] and leaves a[1:lo-1], the converted replacements, then a[hi+1:end].

deleteat!(a, lo:hi) with Int-valued endpoints of any BitInteger type does nothing for an empty range, removes exactly a[lo:hi] for 1 <= lo <= hi <= length(a), and raises BoundsError with a unchanged for a nonempty range outside 1:length(a) whose length is representable.

`reverse!(v, start, stop)` (array.jl:2312; docstring at array.jl:2291-2311: "In-place version of `reverse`") on a vector of the shared heap whose slots may be unassigned, with endpoints of any `Integer` type: an endpoint with no equal `Int` raises `InexactError`; when `stop ≤ start` it returns `v` unchanged; a window `start < stop` reaching outside `1:length(v)` raises `BoundsError` with `v` unchanged; otherwise, when the window `v[start:stop]` is fully assigned it is reversed in place and `v` returned, and when it holds an unassigned slot `UndefRefError` is raised. The midpoint is `midpoint` of array.jl:2283 with the wrapping arithmetic of int.jl.

filter(f, a::Array) of any shape returns a fresh vector of the elements for which f is true, in order, existing arrays unchanged; otherwise the first element in iteration order that is unassigned (UndefRefError), makes f throw, or gives a non-Bool (TypeError) decides the error.

`filter(f, a)` for an abstract array that is not an `Array` (array.jl:3027; docstring at array.jl:2990-3013: "Return a copy of collection `a`, removing elements for which `f` is `false`", with the example `filter(isodd, 1:10)`), for a unit range `lo:hi` of `Int`: when `f` returns a `Bool` for every element, the result is a fresh `Vector{Int}` holding, in order, the elements of the range for which `f` is `true`, the index buffer the call allocates ends empty, and every existing array is unchanged; otherwise the first element on which `f` throws (its error) or returns a non-`Bool` (`TypeError`) decides the error.

deleteat!(a, i) and deleteat!(a, lo:hi) inside 1:length(a) remove exactly those elements; an empty range changes nothing; an out-of-range index is a BoundsError; empty! removes everything.

The first error in any initial phase is returned with exactly its preceding effects. Every successful result is the vector allocated with that key type and native count.

Generic first/last searches propagate pair-construction errors with the exact resulting state before testing any element. Last-search also preserves pair effects before propagating a reverse-iterator-construction error. All typed runtime operations and states are quantified without callee correctness laws.

The selected nonempty homogeneous vect overload allocates a fresh vector containing the argument values in order, preserves existing objects, and reports allocation type or size errors without mutation for the entire machine-sized tuple domain.

Across the existing native type/layout and RefValue interfaces, Array elsize preserves every error, divergence and state effect; a boxed element uses an eight-byte pointer slot, while a valid inline alignment yields the mathematically least sufficient aligned extent.

Ptr elsize handles Any, non-DataTypes and datatype layouts in source order, preserving native errors, divergence and resulting state; valid alignments produce the mathematically least sufficient padded payload size.

For every native-sized Array header projection, sizeof accounts for the mathematical element count times the independently aligned payload stride modulo the native word width, omits union selector bytes, and preserves layout failures and divergence even for empty arrays.
Arrays of the same element type and mathematical element count have the same complete sizeof outcome regardless of shape or rank, including native errors, divergence and final state.

For every Array projection satisfying the necessary native size/window invariants and every machine-sized Int-index tuple, isassigned returns the definedness of the mathematically selected column-major cell, or false for an out-of-bounds tuple, without mutation. The domain includes zero dimensions, no indices, linear indexing, omitted trailing singleton axes, extra singleton indices, shared-memory offsets and undefined reference slots; pointer-free cells are assigned in bounds.

For every valid same-element-type Array pair at every rank, including arbitrary physical overlap, empty source is an exact no-op, short destination raises BoundsError before native effects, and success returns the original destination. Both native branches are constrained by independent mathematical counts and addresses. Non-bits storage reaches its native copy request; bits storage observes raw layout, checked byte-count conversion, memmove and ordered GC ends, preserving every error, partial state and divergence.

For every valid same-element-type Array destination and Memory source, including arbitrary physical overlap, empty source is an exact no-op, short destination raises BoundsError before native effects, and success returns the original destination. Both native branches use the independent count and Memory origin. The bits protocol includes raw layout, signed-byte-count rejection, memmove and ordered GC ends; every success, error, partial state and divergence is constrained.

For every valid same-element-type Memory destination and Array source at every rank, including arbitrary physical overlap, empty source is an exact no-op, short destination raises BoundsError before native effects, and success returns the original destination. Both native branches use independent counts and physical addresses from the Array window to the Memory origin. The bits protocol includes raw layout, signed-byte-count rejection, memmove and ordered GC ends, retaining every error, partial state and divergence.

For every valid native Array at every rank, copy captures the initial source reference, uses the initial shape for checked Memory allocation, rereads its current length after allocation, and rereads its current shape after copying. Independent mathematical counts and native-copy observations constrain all errors, mutations and divergence. A successful Core header action installs exactly the captured final fields at its returned identity and preserves every other header and raw native effect; no callback-preservation or freshness law is assumed.

Every valid Vector source requests exactly its source shape and element type through the actual native allocation/header protocol, retaining all dimension/type/byte-size errors and native effects or divergence.

Every valid Matrix source requests exactly its complete source shape and element type through the actual native allocation/header protocol, retaining all dimension/type/byte-size errors and native effects or divergence.
Every valid Vector source requests its shape with the selected new element type through the native allocation/header protocol, including every type/size/native error, partial state and divergence.

Every valid Matrix source requests its complete shape with the selected new element type through the native allocation/header protocol, including every dimension/type/size/native error, partial state and divergence.

For every native Int length, similar requests a Vector of the source element type and that exact length, with independent negative/zero/native-size rejection and exact native allocation/header outcomes.

For every representable native dimension tuple and selected new element type, similar requests exactly that shape and rank; independent dimension/type/byte-size checks and raw native outcomes determine the complete result.

For every representable native dimension tuple, similar retains the source element type and requests exactly that shape and rank, including all mathematical dimension/type/byte-size errors and native outcomes.

The source Array type rank is discarded: every representable requested dimension tuple selects the result rank and exact shape, retaining the element type and all dimension/type/byte-size/native errors, effects and divergence.

Every constructible nonempty Any-literal argument tuple produces a fresh vector containing exactly those values, preserving their order and reference identities and all previous objects; native-size allocation rejection raises ArgumentError before mutation. Empty calls select the separate source471 overload.

For fill(v, ()), every scalar type and value requests a one-element rank-zero Array, propagates all allocation/native errors and divergence, and returns the constructed Array identity after the exact native fill request. UInt8/Int8 select one memset byte with signed Cint preservation and ordered GC end; every other type requests Core memoryrefnew at index one with false bounds flag, then sends its successful returned reference and the original value to one not_atomic/false Core store. Native partial effects are retained without content or freshness laws.
Unknown-size collection allocation returns a fresh empty vector preserving prior objects, or a type error without mutation for invalid element layout.

The inference-only iterator helper retains initial iterator effects, errors and divergence; an empty protocol result throws nothing and a nonempty result raises TypeError at the non-Bool conditional, without returning a value.
Every native requested capacity uses the source Memory element layout and independent mathematical element/byte-size checks, retaining every native allocation outcome and state.
For all native delta and length values, initial checked length overflow raises OverflowError before mutation; every successful beginning growth returns the reference installed in the final header.
For all native delta and length values, initial checked length overflow in ending growth raises OverflowError before any mutation or native effect.

Both global-constant queries return true exactly when their corresponding libjulia runtime query returns a nonzero C integer.
datatype_haspadding returns what its docstring says.
datatype_fielddesc_type returns the field-descriptor entry size its docstring describes.
datatype_npointers returns an Int, as its docstring signature declares.
Ordered property reads forward the original object, field and memory order to the corresponding global or field operation.
Ordered property writes preserve their memory order, convert values when required, and propagate type-lookup failures; type-object writes raise an error.
Field and global modification forward the operator, operand, memory order and runtime result unchanged.
Field and global swaps convert to the declared type when required, forward the order and return the primitive's old value.
hasfield(T, name) returns a Bool for every type T.
Every type iskindtype accepts is concrete, as its docstring states.
Background-state lock methods delegate to the contained lock with the same callback or unit argument.
Every nonempty tuple of integer index vectors and ranges accepted by get(A, I, default), with no more indices than dimensions, produces its source and destination index positions.
keepat!(a, inds) and keepat!(a, mask) retain the selected slots in order, including unassigned reference slots, and return the modified vector.
Filtering an empty Cartesian-indexed array returns its empty selection without evaluating the predicate, even when the predicate's return type is not inferred to be Bool.
reshape!(a, dims) with the same rank and element count returns the identical array after updating its dimensions.

OS predicates match exactly their kernel symbols, isunix throws on unknown systems, detectwsl needs Linux plus a WSL marker, and the generated zero-argument predicates apply their predicate to KERNEL.

mapslices with empty dims is map(f, A); otherwise the dimensions are validated in order before any slice is taken, and the first one that is not an integer, is below one, or exceeds ndims(A) raises ArgumentError.

Stacking writes the k-th slice at index firstindex(B, dims) + k - 1 along the stacking dimension; map! with one, two or several sources stores each result at the position its operands were read from; keepat! leaves exactly the kept elements in order at the front of the vector, keeping its first index.

reduce(vcat, vs) for a nonempty vector of vectors allocates the native sum of their lengths and fills consecutive slices with the vectors in order; reduce(hcat, vs) for equal-length vectors allocates length(vs[1]) rows and one column per vector and places the k-th vector in column k (one dense copy per vector when all are Arrays, a column assignment otherwise); a second operand with a different row count raises DimensionMismatch before allocation.
A zero-index read, defaulted read, and supported write select the sole element of a lawful IndexLinear vector, including one whose axis is a UnitRange such as 3:3.

With no indices, bounds checking accepts exactly when every axis has length one, a failed check stops reads and writes before index conversion or element access, and the IndexCartesian fallback converts the empty index list to each axis's first index in order, keeping its integer type.

A single Int index is valid exactly within a vector's axis and within 1:length(A) for other linear-indexed arrays, a failed check stops indexing before conversion or element access, and an IndexCartesian array converts a valid linear index to the column-major subscripts that convert back to it.

Several Int indices are accepted exactly when each lies in its axis, omitted dimensions are singleton and extra indices equal one; a failed check stops reads and writes before conversion or element access; and an IndexLinear array reads the value at the converted linear position.

The linear eachindex axis is the vector's own axis and 1:length(A) otherwise: exactly its indices pass the scalar bounds check, and iteration visits each of its positions once from the first index and stops outside it.

copyto!(dest, src) and copyto!(deststyle, dest, srcstyle, src) write every source element in order into the destination prefix for every pair of index styles, with no other assignment, using source data identities and dense unaliasing; a destination too short for the source is rejected before any write.

copyto!(dest, dstart, src, sstart, n) copies exactly n source elements from sstart on to dest from dstart on when n > 0 and both ranges fit; n == 0 returns without writing, a negative n raises ArgumentError, and a start outside either linear axis or too few remaining positions raise BoundsError before any read or write.

copyto!(dest, dstart, src) with an iterable writes its elements to consecutive linear positions from dstart and leaves other cells unchanged, whether or not src has a length; for a sized source and nonempty destination an empty source writes nothing, a failed bounds check at dstart propagates, and too few positions from dstart to lastindex(dest) raise BoundsError before any write.
copyto!(dest, dstart, src, sstart) raises BoundsError when sstart is outside the source's linear axis, and otherwise copies the source from sstart to its last linear index through counted copying.

copyto!(B, ir_dest, jr_dest, A, ir_src, jr_src) raises ArgumentError when the row or column range lengths differ, propagates failed destination and source bounds checks, and otherwise assigns B[ir_dest[p], jr_dest[q]] = A[ir_src[p], jr_src[q]] for every pair, columns outer and rows inner, reading the unaliased source, with no other assignment.

Iterating an array visits, for linear iteration, the element at each axis position from the first index and stops outside the axis, and for Cartesian iteration yields the elements at its index sequence in order, propagating the first failed read.

Bounds checking accepts a single scalar index exactly within the vector's axis or 1:length(A), accepts Cartesian indices exactly when each lies in its axis, omitted dimensions are singleton and extra indices equal one, and accepts no indices exactly when every axis has length one.

map!(f, dest, As...) with one or more source vectors stores f of the k-th elements of the sources in position k of dest for every k that dest and all sources have and leaves the rest unchanged; with no source arrays its assertion is raised.

On Union{Bool,Missing}, &, |, xor, !, and the derived nand/nor forms follow three-valued logic. In particular, missing & false is false, missing | true is true, and a result is missing exactly when changing a missing operand can change its Boolean value.
Three-valued &, |, and ! satisfy commutativity, associativity, De Morgan's laws, and distributivity on Union{Bool,Missing}.
==, !=, <, <=, >, and >= return missing when either operand is missing; with two ordinary values they use the ordinary comparison methods.
isless on values that may be missing is a strict weak order whenever isless on ordinary values is a strict weak order.
isless(missing, x) is false for every x; isless(x, missing) is true for every non-missing x.
For any two possibly-missing values, exactly one of isless(x,y), isless(y,x), or isequal(x,y) is true whenever that trichotomy holds for ordinary values.
isequal treats missing as equal only to missing, and extends any ordinary equivalence relation to values that may be missing.
min and max return missing if either argument is missing, and minmax returns the pair (min(x,y), max(x,y)).
coalesce returns its first non-missing argument, or missing if none exists; @coalesce returns the first non-missing evaluated argument, or missing.
When either arithmetic operand is missing, or the base of an integer power is missing, coalesce skips the result and returns its next non-missing value.
For ordinary type members A and B, nonmissingtype(Union{Missing,A,B}) and eltype(SkipMissing{Union{Missing,A,B}}) are Union{A,B}; nonmissingtype(Any) remains Any.

For a finite list-backed iterator, each iterate(::SkipMissing) call returns the first non-missing value from its remaining state and the suffix after that value; repeated calls yield non-missing values in order.

For a finite list-backed parent iterator, a successful iterate(skipmissing(x)) yields one non-missing value and leaves a suffix whose non-missing count is the remaining number of outputs; exhaustion occurs exactly when the suffix has no non-missing values.

keys(skipmissing(x)) and eachindex(skipmissing(x)) contain exactly the indices whose parent values are non-missing; indexing at such a key returns its value, while indexing an in-bounds missing value throws MissingException.
filter(f, skipmissing(x)) returns exactly the non-missing elements of x for which f returns true, in order.
Indexing skipmissing with a vector of indices never returns a missing value.
findfirst returns the key of the first non-missing key/value pair whose value satisfies the predicate.
findlast over skipmissing returns the last parent index whose non-missing value satisfies the predicate.

For arrays whose element type excludes Missing, mapreduce uses the raw reducer selected by the parent IndexStyle. If the element type includes Missing, linear arrays use the SkipMissing reducer and Cartesian arrays use mapfoldl.
float preserves every non-missing element up to the element's own float conversion.
On the source-backed type model, nonmissingtype_checked rejects Any and Missing, and removes Missing from Union{Missing,T} to return T.
When ispositive, isnegative, or isapprox receives a missing operand, coalesce skips its result and returns the next non-missing value.
A missing unary operand, integer Boolean operand, text-multiplication operand, or round input is skipped by coalesce in favor of its next non-missing value.
Rounding a missing value into a concrete target type raises MissingException with the message recommending Union{T,Missing}.
show prints `missing`, showerror prints `MissingException: ` followed by its message, and show on SkipMissing wraps the parent display in `skipmissing(...)`.

The type-level zero, one, and oneunit methods return missing for Missing and select the underlying type for Union{Missing,T}; Any methods raise MethodError with argument tuple (Any,). Float, real, and complex on Any raise the same error, and on Union{Missing,T} they transform the non-missing type and preserve Missing.

Isinteger is true exactly when the finite value equals a mathematical integer; covers both zeros, negative values, infinities and NaNs.
Isinf is true exactly at the two signed infinite numeric values, excluding every finite value and NaN.
Isnan is true exactly when neither lower nor upper comparison with the extended real endpoints orders the represented value; this states semantic classification, not the exponent-tag test.
Isfinite is true exactly for values strictly between negative and positive infinity in independent numeric order, including both zeros.
Iszero is true exactly for numeric zero, irrespective of its sign, and false for nonzero finite values and all nonfinite values.
Isone is true exactly for mathematical one at any precision, excluding all special values.
Ispositive is true exactly for values mathematically greater than zero, including positive infinity and excluding both zeros and NaNs.
Isnegative is true exactly for values mathematically less than zero, including negative infinity and excluding negative zero and NaNs.
Typemax is an infinite value that is an upper bound under the actual BigFloat <= model for every non-NaN input, at every valid stored precision.
Typemin is an infinite value that is a lower bound under the actual BigFloat <= model for every non-NaN input, at every valid stored precision.

Atomic memory indexing dispatches linear vs subscripted coordinates; Cartesian and boolean-mask checkbounds/checkindex split axis tuples and check endpoints or mask axes; LogicalIndex collects iterator elements and BitArray iteration scans chunks using trailing zeros and low-bit clearing; to_indices and uncolon expand Cartesian, mask, and colon indices; _prechecked_iterate steps unit, linear, Cartesian, and 2D-reshaped cursors; and _getindex/_setindex! check destination sizes and write elements in column-major order.

BitArray contiguous, range, and general gather/scatter/fill copy and fill chunks at computed bit offsets while preserving empty targets; copy_to_bitarray_chunks! validates 0/1 source values via try_bool_conversion; BitArray and generic isassigned check per-dimension bounds and suppress bounds/undef errors; _unique_dims deduplicates slices along valid dimensions and copies out-of-range dimensions; and sortslices uses row permutation on 2D matrices with dims=1 and slice broadcast assignment otherwise.

Integer constructors preserve rank and coordinate positions on the Base path, invoke selected dispatch in source order, preserve mutations and exceptions, and check the stored tuple type after conversion completes. Selected custom constructor returns remain uncoerced.
Every Bool/BitInteger constructor preserves all mathematical coordinates exactly or raises InexactError for an unrepresentable native Int coordinate; it does not wrap or return another type.
Singleton flatten invokes Tuple once on its sole input field, performs no splat, and preserves arbitrary returned or thrown Julia values and mutation.

Flatten converts an input prefix from left to right, delegates any selected custom recursive call exactly the remaining suffix, then assembles actual results by right-associated splats, preserving arguments, terminal errors and mutations.

CartesianIndex display uses one original IO reference and ordered display calls: the opening delimiter, comma-separated coordinate prints or one selected custom join, and the closing delimiter. It preserves partial mutations and arbitrary exceptions, stops at the first failed call, and returns the final print's actual result.

Coordinate indexing preserves primitive-read provenance, tuple/subscript arguments, state mutations, and the first Base or arbitrary user exception; concrete integer branches obey exact numerical position/error invariants and custom tuple-index dispatch is called once.

For every Bool or BitInteger subscript, coordinate indexing returns the original one-based coordinate, raises BoundsError for a representable invalid position, or raises Int64 InexactError before bounds for an unrepresentable subscript.
Every normalized constructible BigInt subscript has exact mathematical coordinate semantics, with Int64 conversion failure preceding bounds; all limb counts and signed values are admitted.
A returning custom tuple-index method preserves every possible native or nonnative result, Base or custom exception, and state mutation; the wrapper does not invent nontermination.
Get-with-default makes one tuple-get call with the original array, coordinates, and default, preserving arbitrary return/error and state effects for every array dispatch and indexing origin.
Every possible return or exception from a total selected tuple-get method is preserved together with its final state, with no coercion to the default's type.

For same-rank concrete CartesianIndices arrays, get returns the unchanged default exactly outside the machine address domain, and otherwise returns coordinates satisfying the independent affine geometry modulo 2^64.

Numeric and tuple CartesianIndex conversions make one selected conversion call on the original target type object and raw stored coordinate or tuple, retaining its arbitrary return, thrown value, and shared-state mutations without a new result assertion.

Converting a rank-one CartesianIndex to Bool or any BitInteger preserves its sole mathematical coordinate and exact requested type when representable; InexactError occurs exactly when that target cannot represent the coordinate.

Conversion to Tuple or a fixed Any/Bool/BitInteger tuple preserves ordered coordinates and exact runtime field types. Incompatible arity raises MethodError before scalar-conversion errors; at equal arity, InexactError occurs exactly when a paired field is unrepresentable.

Range membership observes emptiness/first/step/last in order, scans coordinate positions without decreasing them, fetches at most one candidate, preserves original comparison operands and arbitrary equality returns, and stops at the first exception or non-Bool control predicate while retaining state.
An empty range returns false immediately after the emptiness observation; a non-Bool emptiness value raises TypeError there, preserving its state changes and skipping every later callee.
Rank-zero nonempty membership preserves every value or exception returned by the final custom x==first comparison and its final state, without a fabricated Bool assertion.

On every constructible native CartesianIndex StepRangeLen, membership returns a Bool matching existence of an indexed affine point modulo 2^64, including all offsets, zero/negative strides, rank zero, empty lengths, and overflowing coordinate arithmetic.

Ordinal-range tuple construction preserves the ordered conversion prefix, genuinely selected whole/tail maps and non-tuple splatting, then checks tuple kind, original arity and every OrdinalRangeInt field before constructor dispatch. All completed map effects survive a type-bound error; selected exceptions, mutations and constructor returns remain exact.

Integer normalization preserves its oneto call; unit and ordinal normalization read the original range in source order and pass the exact independently typed first/step/last results to colon. Every error stops later calls and retains prior shared-state mutations; success returns the selected oneto or colon result unchanged.

On InterConditionalsLattice, same-slot InterConditionals merge then and else types below and give InterConditional(slot, then, else) when they differ; different slots give Const(v) for a common known Bool v, else Bool; an InterConditional against a non-InterConditional, non-Const, non-Union{} element is widened and handed down; two non-InterConditionals are handed down unchanged.

On MustAliasesLattice, two same-alias MustAliases whose vartyps widen to === types keep the alias with vartyp and fldtyp merged below (update_mustalias); a MustAlias against a non-alias, non-Union{} element is widened to its fldtyp and handed down; non-aliases are handed down unchanged. The same for InterMustAlias.

On PartialsLattice, past the fast path: PartialStruct/Const pairs that are not === give tmerge_partial_struct's answer; same-type PartialOpaques give PartialOpaque(typ, tmerge(envs), parent, source) when source and parent are the same, else the type; PartialTasks give PartialTask(tmerge(fetch types)) or Task when that is Any; other pairs are handed down unchanged.
On ConstsLattice, unless both are Const/PartialTypeVar and ===, each Const or PartialTypeVar is widened to its type and the pair is merged by JLTypeLattice; other arguments are passed on unchanged.
On JLTypeLattice, two equal concrete types give a; otherwise, when each is concrete or a Type{T}, Union{a, b}; otherwise the tmerge_fast_path answer when there is one, else tmerge_types_slow(a, b).
limit_type_size(t, ...) is t when type_more_complex is false; otherwise r = _limit_type_size(t, compare, ...) when t <: r, else r' = _limit_type_size(t, Any, ...) when t <: r', else Any.
For two different names, tname_intersect is nothing when neither wrapper is abstract; a when the walk up from b meets a; otherwise b when a's ancestor at b's height has name b, else nothing.

issimplertype on Conditional, InterConditional, MustAlias, InterMustAlias, PartialOpaque and PartialTask, branch by branch: same-slot (alias) pairs compare their component types recursively (and issubalias for aliases), a Conditional is simpler than a Const, PartialOpaque is never simpler, and other pairings are false.

A PartialStruct a (not === b, widened type simpler, b a Const or PartialStruct with at least as many initialized fields) is simpler than b exactly when every field is lattice-equal to its declared field type, to its type name's wrapper, or to getfield_tfunc(b, i).
